title: standardize policy serialization, KMS metadata normalizer, and audit TTL hints
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Standardizes RBAC v2 policy serialization to a canonical envelope, normalizes KMS metadata keys across components, and surfaces audit TTL hints for downstream retention tooling.
body:
Summary:
This PR standardizes how RBAC v2 policies are serialized across the control plane and the installer, normalizes KMS-related metadata fields so downstream consumers (audit, billing, installers) receive consistent keys, and exposes optional audit TTL hints on policy envelopes to help compliance tooling make retention decisions. The goal is to reduce drift between hosted and private deployments and remove a class of subtle mismatches that trigger noisy audit alerts and failed installer validations.

Motivation and context:
- Multiple teams have shipped policy mutations with slightly different key casing and optional fields (e.g., kmsKeyRegion vs kms_region) which forced fragile parsing in the audit forwarder and private installer.
- The installer validation rejected a small percentage of customer manifests during upgrades due to missing normalized KMS attributes.
- Compliance requested a non-binding TTL hint on audit entries tied to policy changes to allow retention pipelines to group and age policy-change events more predictably (ENG-1294).

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a canonical PolicyEnvelope serializer (pkg/policy/serialize/canonical.go) used by the API server, installer, and rbac-cli. The envelope standardizes field names and types for all top-level attributes.
- Implements a KMS Metadata Normalizer (pkg/kms/metadata_normalizer.go) that maps legacy keys to canonical names and validates region/account formatting.
- Adds an optional audit.ttl_hint field to the envelope (ISO8601 duration string, e.g., PT720H) that is forwarded to the audit pipeline but does not change the system retention defaults.
- Updates the private-installer manifest adapter to call the normalizer before validation so installer errors are deterministic.
- Adds unit and integration tests covering round-trip serialization, legacy key normalization, and audit TTL parsing.

Checklist:
- [x] API server and CLI use the same serializer
- [x] Normalizer translation table covers known legacy keys used in the last 18 months
- [x] Installer validation updated to accept canonicalized envelopes
- [x] Audit pipeline forwards ttl_hint as metadata but ignores it when unset
- [x] Backwards-compatible: legacy envelopes are accepted and normalized on ingest
- [x] Documentation updated: docs/security/rbacv2_serialization.md

Commits (summary):
- feat(policy): add canonical PolicyEnvelope serializer and tests (4 commits)
- feat(kms): implement metadata normalizer and translation table
- fix(installer): adapt manifest adapter to call normalizer before validation
- test: add integration test against installer adapter and audit forwarder stub
- docs: add RBAC v2 serialization guide and migration notes

Files changed (high-level):
- pkg/policy/serialize/canonical.go (new) - implements canonical envelope and JSON schema
- pkg/policy/serialize/schema.json (new) - machine-readable schema for CI validation
- pkg/kms/metadata_normalizer.go (new) - translation table and validators
- cmd/installer/adapter/manifest_adapter.go - call normalizer and simplify error messages
- api/handlers/policy_create.go - switch to canonical serializer for persisted objects
- docs/security/rbacv2_serialization.md - guide and migration steps
- test/integration/policy_roundtrip_test.go - integration tests
- internal/audit/forwarder_stub.go - updated to accept ttl_hint metadata

Small illustrative snippet (serializer canonical envelope):
{
  "envelope_version": "1.0",
  "policy_id": "pol_abc123",
  "spec": { /* policy document */ },
  "kms_metadata": {
    "provider": "aws-kms",
    "key_arn": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd",
    "region": "us-west-2"
  },
  "audit": {
    "actor": "system:operator",
    "ttl_hint": "P30D"
  }
}

Backward compatibility strategy:
- At the API ingress we accept legacy keys and pass them through the normalizer. This keeps the public API backwards-compatible; clients do not need immediate changes.
- The new canonical serializer is used when persisting objects and when emitting policy-change audit events. That means the canonical form will be present in persisted state after the next update to an existing policy.
- A migration helper CLI (rbac-cli migrate-serialize) is included in this PR to bulk-rewrite persisted policies on-demand.

Review conversation (selected):
- Omar Patel (reviewer): "The schema looks good. My only concern is that ttl_hint can be misinterpreted as mandatory retention. Can we make the docs very explicit that ttl_hint is advisory?"
  - Maya Chen (author): "Agreed. Updated docs/security/rbacv2_serialization.md to emphasize advisory semantics and added an explicit example where it is ignored. Also added a test to ensure audit pipeline treats ttl_hint as metadata only."

- Leah Rivera (reviewer): "Installer validation now depends on the normalizer. If the normalizer has a bug it could hide real validation issues. Can we add a CI gate to run schema validation before and after normalizer in a smoke test?"
  - Maya Chen: "Done. Added a small smoke test in test/integration/installer_normalizer_smoke_test.go and a GitHub Actions step that executes it on the installer matrix."

- Jonas Kline (approver): "Verified behavior on a staging cluster. Normalization correctly reconciles legacy keys and the installer no longer rejects manifests. Left one nit about a log message."
  - Maya Chen: "Addressed the nit (changed log level to debug for expected normalization events)."

CI history:
- Initial run (linux/go-1.20 matrix): failed - linter (gofmt) and one unit test that expected legacy key to remain unchanged.
- Fix 1: run gofmt and update unit test to assert normalization; re-run CI.
- Secondary run: failed - installer smoke test on macOS runner due to flaky timing in test harness. Marked test as retryable and added a small wait in harness.
- Final run: all checks passed (unit, integration, linter, e2e smoke).

Migration notes and rollout plan:
1) Deploy API server with canonical serializer and normalizer (no breaking changes).
2) Deploy installer update that uses the same normalizer.
3) Monitor audit-forwarder and installer logs for normalization debug entries for one deployment window (48 hours).
4) Offer opt-in bulk migration via rbac-cli for customers that want persisted canonical envelopes immediately.
5) After 30 days of monitoring, enable a background job that opportunistically rewrites persisted policies to canonical form (feature flagged).

Security and compliance considerations:
- KMS metadata normalization includes stricter validation on key ARNs and region names to reduce accidental misrouting of CMK operations.
- Normalizer logs are debug by default to avoid leaking KMS identifiers into high-volume logs; we added a redaction helper used by audit-forwarder.
- TTL hints do not affect retention policies in the control plane; compliance tooling may choose to honor the hint but must do its own authorization checks.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Expose canonical envelope schema version in the persisted object metadata so future schema evolution is explicit (ENG-1302).
- Add compatibility checks to the Private installer upgrade path to surface possible normalization mismatches earlier.

Merge outcome:
- PR reviewed by Omar, Leah, and Jonas. All comments addressed. CI green. Merged to main via squash on 2026-02-18.

If you'd like, I can extract the canonical schema into a small standalone repo for compliance teams to consume, or prepare a short migration runbook for customers upgrading self-hosted deployments.
